questions.text: Explain the basic block diagram of a digital computer. Differentiate between Microprocessor and Microcontroller with architecture and applications.
Explain the Stored Program Concept (Von Neumann architecture) and the Bus Organization (Address, Data, and Control buses) of a computer system.
Explain the processing cycle (Fetch, Decode, Execute) of a stored program computer system with a flow diagram.

Explain the internal architecture of Intel 8085 microprocessor with a neat functional block diagram. Explain the functions of ALU, General Purpose Registers (B, C, D, E, H, L), Program Counter (PC), Stack Pointer (SP), and Flag Register (S, Z, AC, P, CY).
Explain Demultiplexing of the Address/Data Bus ($AD_0-AD_7$) in 8085 using 74LS373 latch and the ALE signal. Draw the bus timing diagram for Opcode Fetch Machine Cycle (e.g. MOV A, M).
Explain the Addressing Modes of 8085 (Immediate, Direct, Register, Register Indirect, Implicit) with code examples.
Write an 8085 Assembly Language Program (ALP) to sort an array of 10 bytes stored from memory location 2050H in ascending order using Bubble Sort.
Write an 8085 ALP to find the largest and smallest number from a block of N bytes stored starting from 3000H.
Write an 8085 ALP to generate a time delay of 100 ms using nested loops. Show accurate calculation of T-states assuming 3 MHz crystal frequency.
Explain the internal architecture of Intel 8086 microprocessor. Differentiate between Bus Interface Unit (BIU) and Execution Unit (EU). Explain the benefits of Instruction Pipelining in 8086.

Explain Memory Segmentation in 8086 (Code, Data, Stack, Extra Segments). Calculate the 20-bit Physical Address given Segment Address `2000H` and Offset Address `0150H` ($Physical = Segment \times 10H + Offset$).
Explain Minimum Mode vs Maximum Mode of 8086. Explain functions of pins: $MN/\overline{MX}$, $HOLD$, $HLDA$, $LOCK$, and $\overline{TEST}$.
Explain 8086 Assembly Language Syntax: Directives (DB, DW, DD, SEGMENT, ENDS, ASSUME, PROC, ENDP), Statements, and Operators. Differentiate between EXE and COM programs.
Write an 8086 ALP to reverse a given string and check whether it is a Palindrome or not using INT 21H DOS function calls.
Explain Address Decoding techniques: Absolute (Unique) Decoding vs Linear Select (Non-Unique / Partial) Decoding with diagrams.
Interface 8 KB EPROM (2764) and 8 KB SRAM (6264) with 8085 microprocessor starting at address 0000H and 8000H respectively using 74LS138 (3-to-8 decoder). Show memory map and circuit schematic.

Explain 8255 Programmable Peripheral Interface (PPI) block diagram, Operating Modes (Mode 0: Basic I/O, Mode 1: Strobed I/O, Mode 2: Bidirectional Bus), and Control Word formats (I/O mode and BSR mode).
Explain Interrupt Structure of 8085: Hardware Interrupts (TRAP, RST 7.5, RST 6.5, RST 5.5, INTR) in order of priority, trigger type (edge/level), vector addresses, and SIM / RIM instructions.
Explain 8086 Interrupt Processing Sequence and Interrupt Vector Table (IVT). Differentiate between Hardware Interrupts (NMI, INTR) and Software Interrupts (INT n).
Explain 8259 Programmable Interrupt Controller (PIC) architecture and Initialization Command Words (ICW1-ICW4) in cascading mode.
Differentiate between Synchronous and Asynchronous Serial Data Transmission. Explain Baud Rate and framing in serial communication.

Explain Serial Interface Standards: RS-232C standard (voltage levels, handshaking signals RxD, TxD, RTS, CTS, DTR, DSR) and USB. Explain Universal Synchronous Asynchronous Receiver Transmitter (USART 8251) architecture.
